value_domain: Age in completed years at the start of the financial year
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The payee's age in completed years on 1 July, the first day of the financial year the payment summary reports. It is derived by the ABS from date of birth rather than reported by the employer, and the 2020-21 table names the same column age at the start of the reference period. Because it is fixed at 1 July, a person is one year younger here than they are for most of the payments on the row.
value_definition: A whole number of years with no fractional part, constant for a person within a year table and rising by one between consecutive year tables.
limitation: It is not age at the payment, at the job start or at the extract, so it cannot be used to place someone either side of a birthday-linked threshold such as the preservation age or the seniors offset age. A payment summary covering only part of the year still carries the 1 July age, so short spells are aged as though they began in July.
rationale: The ABS assembles PLIDA from linked administrative records and derives demographic columns such as age; no ATO payment summary label carries an age, so the column can only be a derived one, and its name and the sibling wording in the 2020-21 table fix the reference date.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the age is fixed at the start of the year rather than measured when the payments were made.

value_domain: Age in completed years at 1 July 2021
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The payee's age in completed years at the start of the 2021-22 financial year, in the file extracted 16 months after that year closed. It is a derived demographic column, not a label on the payment summary, and it is paired with the age at the end of the same year so a birthday inside the year can be seen. A person shown as 64 here may have spent most of the year at 65.
value_definition: A whole number of years measured at 1 July 2021, one value per person per row, with no code list.
limitation: The pair of start and end ages narrows a birthday to a year, not to a date, so it cannot be used to work out how much of the year's pay fell either side of an age threshold. The column exists only in the 2021-22 tables, so an age series across years has to be rebuilt from differently named columns.
rationale: The column name carries both the financial year and the endpoint, and the table is the 2021-22 payment summary file; the ABS derives this kind of demographic column when it assembles PLIDA rather than taking it from the form.
supersedes_rationale: The entry had no custodian description at all and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing said which year the age was measured in or which end of it.

value_domain: Age in completed years at 30 June 2022
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The payee's age in completed years at the close of the 2021-22 financial year, the companion to the age recorded at the start of that year. Where the two differ by one, the person had a birthday during 2021-22; where they agree, the birthday falls outside the file's window. Like its partner it is derived from date of birth by the ABS rather than reported by the employer.
value_definition: A whole number of years measured at 30 June 2022, equal to the start-of-year age or one greater.
limitation: It is not age at the last payment: the summary period often ends before 30 June, so a person who left a job in September is still aged here at the following June. Nor does it establish residence or presence in Australia at that date, since the row records a payment, not a person's location.
rationale: The column name carries the financial year and the endpoint, and it sits beside the start-of-year age in the same 2021-22 table, which is what makes the pair readable as a birthday indicator.
supersedes_rationale: The entry had no custodian description at all and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing distinguished it from the age at the start of the same year.

value_domain: Age in completed years at 1 July 2022
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The payee's age in completed years at the start of the 2022-23 financial year, in the file extracted 12 months after that year closed. The custodian labels it age start of 2223, and it repeats for 2022-23 the paired age design used in the 2021-22 tables. It is derived from date of birth, so it is present even for rows where the employer reported little else.
value_definition: A whole number of years measured at 1 July 2022. It is carried on both the 6-month and the 12-month extracts of 2022-23, so the same person's age appears twice if the two are stacked.
limitation: A twelve-month extract catches only the payment summaries lodged by then, so the population this age describes is not the same as the population in a longer extract of the same year, and age distributions from the two are not directly comparable. The column also cannot be joined to the 2021-22 age columns by name.
rationale: The custodian's label names the year and the endpoint, and the column sits in the 12-month extract of the 2022-23 payment summary file.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which day of the 2022-23 year the age refers to or that it is derived rather than reported.

value_domain: Age in completed years at 30 June 2023
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The payee's age in completed years at the close of the 2022-23 financial year, labelled age end of 2223 by the custodian. Subtracting the start-of-year age gives a one or a zero, which is the only birthday signal in the table. The topic tagging calls it income, which is wrong: nothing about the payments on the row enters this column.
value_definition: A whole number of years measured at 30 June 2023, either equal to the 1 July 2022 age on the same row or one greater, and repeated across the 6-month and 12-month extracts.
limitation: An age at the end of a financial year says nothing about whether the person was still employed then, because the payment summary period may have closed months earlier. Reading it as age at last payment therefore ages short spells upward, and the error grows the earlier in the year the job ended.
rationale: The custodian's label names the year and the endpoint, and the column pairs with the start-of-year age in the same 2022-23 table.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that this is the later of the two ages on the row and that it carries no income content despite the income tag.

value_domain: Payment summary amendment indicator
value_source: ATO, Correct a mistake, PAYG withholding payment summaries
variable_description: Says whether this payment summary is an original report or an amended one replacing a report already sent for the same payee and year. The ATO sets the values in the annual report file: "In the Amendment indicator field in your annual report file, type: 'A' for Amended payee records 'O' for original records not previously sent to us." Employers amend when they find a wrong tax file number, dollar amount, payment type or code, so a marked row usually means a corrected dollar figure.
value_definition: A single-character code carried on every payment summary record, A for an amended payee record and O for an original one not previously reported.
limitation: It does not say what changed or which earlier row it supersedes, and the amended summary repeats the payee and payer details rather than reversing the earlier amounts. Both rows can therefore sit in the same file, so totalling gross payments by person and year without filtering on this code double counts the amended employment.
rationale: The ATO page on correcting payment summaries names the amendment indicator field, gives its two values and lists the mistakes that trigger an amended record, which is the field this column carries.
evidence_quote: In the Amendment indicator field in your annual report file, type: 'A' for Amended payee records 'O' for original records not previously sent to us.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said what the code distinguishes or that unfiltered totals double count amended rows.

value_domain: Confidentialised business identifier for the payer
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The employer or payer that issued the payment summary, as a confidentialised business identifier assigned by the ABS. In the later extracts it takes the place of the hashed and truncated ABN that the earlier payment summary tables carry, so a payer series that spans the change has to bridge the two columns. It is what makes an employee's job history readable: rows sharing a person and a payer are one employment relationship.
value_definition: An opaque identifier, stable within the asset, standing for a business rather than for an ABN. It is generated in fplida rather than derived from any real business.
limitation: A business identifier is not a workplace or a job. A large employer with many sites shows as one value, a person with two summaries from the same payer in a year is not two jobs, and a business that restructures can change identifier without any change to the employment.
rationale: The same column name in the registry's business and income products carries the custodian's fuller wording, an ABS derived confidentialised business identifier that took over from the hashed ABN, and in the payment summary tables it appears exactly where the hashed ABN drops out.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the column identifies the paying employer or that it stands in for the hashed ABN used in the earlier tables.

value_domain: PLIDA person linkage key (synthetic)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The person the payment summary was issued to, and the key that stitches a year's summaries into one worker's income. A person can have several rows in a single year, one for each payer and payment summary type, so this column has to be aggregated before a row becomes a person-year. ABS holds the joining information away from the data itself: "The Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data."
value_definition: An opaque synthetic number, one value per person, consistent across the payment summary tables and across the other products in the asset. In fplida the values are generated rather than derived from anyone.
limitation: Absence is not absence of work. The file records what payers reported, so a person paid only exempt foreign employment income, or paid by an employer that reported through Single Touch Payroll instead of a payment summary, can be missing for a year in which they were employed throughout.
rationale: ABS describes the person linkage spine and its separation from the data, which is what this key is; the several-rows-per-person structure is visible in the payment summary tables themselves.
evidence_quote: The Person Linkage Spine allows us to link datasets through a spine of key information, separate from the main body of data.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that a person carries several rows in a year, one per payer and form type.

value_domain: Australian financial year of the extract (1 July to 30 June)
value_source: ABS, Person Level Integrated Data Asset (PLIDA)
variable_description: The financial year that the payment summary file itself covers, constant within a table and set by which year's annual reports the ATO extracted. It is the outer frame for the row, while the income year column repeats the year written on the form and the period dates say how much of that year the payments span. Its value earns its keep once several year tables are stacked, because it is what the stacked rows are ordered by.
value_definition: A financial year label rather than a date. It appears only in the 2020-21 and later extracts, where several tables can share a year and differ only in how long after 30 June the file was cut.
limitation: It is not a measure of when income was received, and it does not stand for a complete year of reporting: the 6-month, 12-month and 16-month extracts of the same financial year hold different numbers of summaries, so counts by this column depend on how long after year end the file was cut.
rationale: The column is constant within each table and matches the table name, and the asset is built by the ABS from annual ATO extracts, so it identifies the extract's reference year rather than anything on the form.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the value is constant within a table or how it differs from the income year on the same row.

value_domain: Financial year the payment summary reports (income year)
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - superannuation income stream, How to complete this form
variable_description: The income year written on the payment summary itself, the year ending 30 June that the payments belong to. The ATO tells payers to write it as four digits: "Show the year as a four-digit figure. For example, show the year ending 30 June 2019 as 2019 (and not 19)." It normally matches the extract's financial year, and a row where it does not is a summary reported late or reported for an earlier year.
value_definition: A four-digit year identifying a 1 July to 30 June period, taken from the year field at the top of the payment summary form.
limitation: It cannot date a payment inside the year, and it is not the year the employer lodged. A payer who reports several years of arrears in one lodgment writes each year here, so this column tells you which year the money belongs to and nothing about when it was reported or paid.
rationale: The ATO instructions for completing a payment summary specify the year field and its format, and the ATO glossary defines an income year as a 12-month period ending 30 June.
evidence_quote: Show the year as a four-digit figure. For example, show the year ending 30 June 2019 as 2019 (and not 19).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that this year comes from the form rather than from the extract.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the gross payments label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Everything the employer paid the payee as ordinary salary and wages for the period, before any tax was taken out. The ATO defines the label as "all salary, wages, bonuses and commissions you paid your payee as an employee, company director or office holder" and adds "Include the total gross amount before amounts are withheld". It excludes anything shown in its own column, because employers are told not to include allowances, lump sums, CDEP payments or reportable fringe benefits here.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount, gross of tax withheld. It includes non-superannuation pensions and annuities, compensation, sickness or accident pay, holiday pay and post-1993 leave paid on an ordinary resignation.
limitation: It understates what the job cost the employer and what the worker gave up: salary sacrificed amounts are not in it, superannuation guarantee contributions never appear on the form, and the allowance, lump sum and fringe benefit columns hold pay that this figure deliberately leaves out. Adding those columns to it is the only way to get near total remuneration.
rationale: The ATO instruction for completing the payment summary defines what the gross payments label must contain and lists what must be shown elsewhere instead.
evidence_quote: Include all salary, wages, bonuses and commissions you paid your payee as an employee, company director or office holder. Include the total gross amount before amounts are withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the figure is gross of withholding and excludes the amounts carried in the neighbouring columns.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the total tax withheld label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The tax the payer took out of these payments and sent to the ATO during the year. The instruction is simply to "Show the total tax withheld in whole dollars", and it covers everything on the form, since the ATO adds that "You must include all amounts you withheld from lump sum payments in the total tax withheld". It is money already paid towards the payee's bill, not the bill itself.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount covering withholding from the gross payments, allowances and lump sums shown on the same summary.
limitation: Withholding is not tax on this income. It is an instalment set by tax tables against the payee's declared circumstances, so it is too high for someone with large deductions and too low for someone with a second job, and the assessment settles the difference. An effective tax rate built from this column and gross payments is therefore a withholding rate, not a tax rate.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the total tax withheld label and states that lump sum withholding is included in it.
evidence_quote: You must include all amounts you withheld from lump sum payments in the total tax withheld.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is an instalment covering every payment on the form rather than the tax finally assessed.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the total allowances label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The total of separately itemised allowances the employer paid to cover the payee's work expenses, kept out of gross payments. The ATO defines them as "payments you made to cover your payee's work-related expenses. For example, tool allowances and motor vehicle allowances (including car expense payments on a cents-per-kilometre basis)", and instructs that "You must show the total amount of all allowances you paid in the Total allowances field. Do not include these amounts in gross payments."
value_definition: A whole-dollar total of the allowances listed on the form. Up to two allowance types are named individually; beyond that the payer prints VARIOUS and shows only the sum here.
limitation: It is not all allowances. Allowances that compensate for working conditions or cover expenses the payee cannot deduct are folded into gross payments instead, and living-away-from-home allowance is left off the form altogether, so this column captures only the deductible-expense kind. The type of allowance is also lost once a payer has more than two.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines what an allowance is for this label, states that the total goes here rather than in gross payments, and describes the VARIOUS convention that collapses the types.
evidence_quote: You must show the total amount of all allowances you paid in the Total allowances field. Do not include these amounts in gross payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that some allowances are reported inside gross payments instead and that the types collapse to VARIOUS.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the exempt foreign employment income label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Foreign employment income the employer paid that is exempt from Australian tax, reported apart from gross payments. The ATO states plainly that "Income from foreign employment is exempt from tax if your payee meets certain conditions", and no tax is withheld from it. Where it is all a payer paid there is no form at all: "If the only income you have paid is exempt foreign employment income, you do not need to provide a payment summary."
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount of employment income exempted under the foreign service rules, reported separately from the gross payments on the same summary.
limitation: Exempt does not mean irrelevant. The amount is used to work out the rate applied to the payee's other income, so treating it as untaxed and setting it aside understates the effective rate on the rest. Coverage is also incomplete by design, because a payer whose only payments to a person were exempt foreign employment income need issue no summary at all, so those workers leave no row.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the payment summary names the label, states the exemption condition and gives the case in which no summary is issued at all.
evidence_quote: If the only income you have paid is exempt foreign employment income, you do not need to provide a payment summary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is exempt income reported outside gross payments, or that some exempt income never reaches the file.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the reportable employer superannuation contributions label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Extra superannuation the employer put in at the employee's request, most often under salary sacrifice, over and above the compulsory contributions. The ATO limits the label to influenced contributions: "Complete this section if you paid employer contributions to a super fund at the request of the employee", and it is "not included in your payee's assessable income" even though the payee must report it. It is the counterpart to the gap in gross payments left by sacrificed salary.
value_definition: A whole-dollar cash value of the contribution for the income year 1 July to 30 June, excluding superannuation guarantee amounts, contributions required by a fund's governing rules or by state law, and contributions under a collectively negotiated industrial agreement.
limitation: It is not employer superannuation. Compulsory contributions are far larger for most workers and appear nowhere on the payment summary, so this column cannot measure superannuation coverage or contribution levels. A blank is also ambiguous in the earlier years of the collection, because the reporting requirement did not exist for the whole period the payment summary tables cover.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the label, lists what does and does not count as a reportable contribution, and states that the amount is outside assessable income while still being reported by the payee.
evidence_quote: Reportable employer super contributions are not included in your payee's assessable income; however: you must report them to us as part of your annual payment summary reporting your payee must report them to us in their tax return.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount excludes compulsory contributions or that it sits outside assessable income while still counting in income tests.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the reportable fringe benefits label (grossed up)
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The grossed-up value of fringe benefits the employer provided, shown only where the benefits pass the reporting threshold. The ATO sets the test as: "Complete this section if the total taxable value of certain fringe benefits you provided to your payee in the fringe benefits tax (FBT) year (1 April to 31 March) exceeds $2,000 for the FBT year." An employee whose benefits fall under the threshold shows nothing here, and an employer eligible for exemption from FBT under section 57A ticks a Yes indicator box beside the amount on the same summary.
value_definition: A whole-dollar grossed-up taxable value for the FBT year, reported on the payment summary for the corresponding financial year and excluded from gross payments.
limitation: The figure is not the cash value of the benefit, because grossing up inflates it to the pre-tax salary equivalent, so treating it as remuneration in dollars overstates the benefit by the gross-up factor. Its reference period is also the FBT year to 31 March, which does not line up with the income year on the same row, and benefits below the threshold are invisible, so a zero does not mean no fringe benefits.
rationale: The ATO instruction gives the threshold, the FBT year the value is measured over, the grossing-up requirement and the section 57A indicator box shown beside the amount.
evidence_quote: You must record the grossed-up taxable value of those benefits on your payee's payment summary for the financial year that corresponds with the reportable fringe benefits amount.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is grossed up, threshold-dependent and measured over a year that ends on 31 March.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the Lump sum A label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Unused leave paid out at the end of a job, in the categories the ATO taxes at a concessional flat rate. The label covers "unused long service leave that accrued after 15 August 1978, but before 18 August 1993" and pre-August 1993 holiday pay, plus any post-1993 leave paid alongside a genuine redundancy, early retirement scheme payment or invalidity payment. The type code beside it says which: R for redundancy, invalidity or early retirement, T for everything else.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount excluded from gross payments and paired with a one-character type code in the Lump sum A type column.
limitation: It is not the whole of a person's unused leave payout. Leave that accrued after 17 August 1993 and was paid on an ordinary resignation goes into gross payments instead, so a departing worker's leave is split between two columns according to when it accrued and why they left. The amount also pools accrual vintages taxed at different rates without saying which applies.
rationale: The ATO instruction table for the payment summary sets out exactly which unused leave belongs at Lump sum A, which belongs in gross payments, and what the paired type code means.
evidence_quote: For other amounts of unused leave accrued after 17 August 1993, see gross payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which leave belongs at this label or that the rest of a person's leave payout sits in gross payments.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the Lump sum B label
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 3 Employer lump sum payments
variable_description: Unused long service leave that accrued before 16 August 1978 and was paid out on termination, of which only a twentieth is taxed. The payment summary instruction limits the label to leave that accrued before that date, and the return then cuts the figure down: the taxpayer adds up the Lump sum B amounts and is told to "Divide the total by 20. This is because only 5% is taxable." The summary therefore shows an amount twenty times larger than the income that reaches the assessment.
value_definition: A whole-dollar gross amount of pre-16 August 1978 long service leave, reported separately from gross payments and from Lump sum A.
limitation: The column will not reconcile with the person's return: the return carries five per cent of it, so joining payment summary amounts to assessed income without the divide-by-twenty step overstates income by the difference. Only workers with unbroken service from the 1970s can have any value here, so it is close to empty in the later years and is not a general measure of long service leave.
rationale: The ATO payment summary instruction defines the accrual period for this label and the return instruction states the five per cent inclusion rule that separates the reported amount from taxable income.
evidence_quote: Divide the total by 20. This is because only 5% is taxable.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the label covers only pre-1978 long service leave or that just five per cent of it is taxed.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the Lump sum D label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The tax-free slice of a genuine redundancy or early retirement scheme payment, which the payee never declares. The ATO defines the label as "The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment", and the return instructions for question 3 tell taxpayers to leave these amounts out because no tax is payable on them. A non-zero value is the clearest redundancy marker on the payment summary.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount capped by the statutory tax-free limit, which depends on completed years of service and is indexed each year. It is excluded from gross payments and carries no withholding.
limitation: It measures the concession, not the payout. Anything above the tax-free limit becomes an employment termination payment reported on a different form, so a large redundancy can show a modest figure here and the rest elsewhere, and two workers with identical severance show different amounts because their years of service differ. It also cannot distinguish a genuine redundancy from an early retirement scheme.
rationale: The ATO payment summary instruction defines the label as the tax-free component of a genuine redundancy or early retirement scheme payment, and the return instruction confirms the payee does not declare it.
evidence_quote: The tax-free component of a genuine redundancy payment or an early retirement scheme payment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is the tax-free part only, with the balance reported as an employment termination payment.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the Lump sum E label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: Back pay for work done more than a year earlier, plus return-to-work payments, kept apart so the payee can get the lump sum in arrears offset. The ATO defines the label as "Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments". The return sends it to a different question from ordinary wages: employer lump sum payments in arrears are declared at question 24 Other income rather than at the salary questions.
value_definition: A whole-dollar amount excluded from gross payments, covering salary and wage arrears that accrued more than twelve months before payment.
limitation: It does not say which years the arrears belong to or how many, so it cannot be spread back over the years the work was done, and the offset it triggers depends on that spread. Because it is declared at the other income question, an earnings measure built from gross payments alone silently drops it in exactly the years a back-pay settlement lands.
rationale: The ATO payment summary instruction defines the label and the return instruction states where the payee declares it, which is what separates it from ordinary wages.
evidence_quote: Amounts you paid for back payment of salary or wages that accrued more than 12 months ago or any return to work payments.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount is arrears for earlier years or that it is declared at the other income question.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the tax-free component label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - superannuation income stream, How to complete this form
variable_description: The tax-free part of a superannuation income stream or termination payment on this row, which the payee is not taxed on. For a pension the ATO builds it from the member's own after-tax money: "For super income streams from 1 July 2007, the tax-free component is made up of the: contributions segment crystallised segment." The payment summary type column on the same row says which form the row came from, and ordinary salary and wage summaries leave this column empty.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component amount reported on the superannuation income stream and employment termination payment summaries, sitting beside the taxable component of the same payment.
limitation: A blank means a different form, not a nil component, so counting blanks as zeros mixes wage earners into a population of pension recipients. It is also a different concept from the Lump sum D tax-free redundancy amount that can appear on the same row, and the two must not be added as though they were one tax-free total.
rationale: The ATO instruction for completing the superannuation income stream payment summary defines the tax-free component and its two segments, and the same component appears on the employment termination payment summary that this pooled table also carries.
evidence_quote: For super income streams from 1 July 2007, the tax-free component is made up of the: contributions segment crystallised segment.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which payments carry a tax-free component or how it differs from the Lump sum D amount.

value_domain: Dollar amount at the taxable component label
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - superannuation income stream, How to complete this form
variable_description: The assessable part of a superannuation income stream or termination payment on this row - the part that is taxed. The ATO notes that "The taxable component of a super benefit may consist of a taxed element and/or an untaxed element, depending on whether the benefit is paid from a taxed or untaxed source", and the two elements are taxed differently. For a termination payment the return uses this figure directly: the payee writes the taxable component of the ETP at the ETP label with its code.
value_definition: A whole-dollar component amount that, with the tax-free component beside it, sums to the payment reported on that summary. It may combine a taxed and an untaxed element.
limitation: The single figure hides the split between the taxed and untaxed elements, so the tax actually payable cannot be worked out from it without knowing the source of the benefit and the payee's age. It is also not comparable with gross payments on wage rows, because a termination payment or pension is taxed under its own schedule rather than at marginal rates.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the superannuation income stream payment summary defines the taxable component and its elements, and the return instruction for employment termination payments shows the same component being carried into the assessment.
evidence_quote: The taxable component of a super benefit may consist of a taxed element and/or an untaxed element, depending on whether the benefit is paid from a taxed or untaxed source.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the amount combines a taxed and an untaxed element or that it belongs to the pension and termination forms rather than to wages.

value_domain: Date (start of the payment summary period)
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The first day of the span the payment summary covers, as the payer chose to state it. The ATO asks for the period rather than pay dates: "Show the period during which the payments were made to your worker or payee", and for a full year of employment "show the period as 1 July 2014 to 30 June 2015". It is deliberately loose - employers are told "You do not need to show the first and last pay dates for the financial year in this field."
value_definition: A calendar date within the income year on the same row, paired with the period end date to bound the payments reported on the form.
limitation: It is not a job start date. A person hired in March may be shown from 1 July, and casuals paid at scattered times through the year are told to show the whole financial year, so a spell length built from this column overstates short and irregular employment. It also cannot be compared across payers, since each states the period its own way.
rationale: The ATO instruction for the payment summary defines what the period fields must show, gives the full-year convention and states that first and last pay dates are not required.
evidence_quote: You do not need to show the first and last pay dates for the financial year in this field.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the date bounds a reported period rather than marking when the job began.

value_domain: Date (end of the payment summary period)
value_source: ATO, PAYG payment summary - individual non-business, Section B: Payment details
variable_description: The last day of the span the payment summary covers, which for a continuing job is simply 30 June. The ATO's instruction for casual work is what makes it unreliable as a leaving date: if the payee worked "over various times for the whole year, show the period as the whole financial year", and if they worked only part of the year, "write the period of the year the payments were made over". A date before 30 June therefore suggests, but does not prove, that the job ended.
value_definition: A calendar date within the income year on the same row, not earlier than the period start date on the same summary.
limitation: It cannot be read as a termination date. Payers use it for the last pay period, for the end of a contract and for the end of the year alike, and a job that ends in early July shows a 30 June date in the earlier year's file. Length of employment inferred from the two period dates is therefore an upper bound rather than a measure.
rationale: The ATO instruction defines the period fields and gives the casual and part-year conventions that decide what an early end date means.
evidence_quote: during the year, write the period of the year the payments were made over over various times for the whole year, show the period as the whole financial year.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that a date short of 30 June reflects the reported period rather than a recorded job ending.

value_domain: Date of payment on a single-payment summary
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments
variable_description: The date of the payment itself, carried by the payment summary types that report one payment rather than a year of them. An employment termination payment summary is the main case, and the return takes the date straight off it: "Write at Date of payment the payment date on your income statement or payment summary." It sits beside the period start and end dates, which serve the ordinary salary and wage summaries instead.
value_definition: A calendar date on the summary, present for the payment summary types that report a discrete payment and absent where the form reports a period.
limitation: A blank here is a form type, not a missing value, so treating blanks as unknown dates confuses wage summaries with incomplete records. The date also fixes when the payment was made rather than what it was for: a termination payment made in July belongs to the new income year even though the employment ended in the old one.
rationale: The ATO return instruction for employment termination payments shows the date of payment being read off the payment summary, which is the field the earlier tables name in this way.
evidence_quote: Write at Date of payment the payment date on your income statement or payment summary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said which payment summary types carry a payment date or why the field is empty on ordinary wage rows.

value_domain: Date of payment on a single-payment summary (later naming)
value_source: ATO, Individual tax return instructions 2025, question 4 Employment termination payments
variable_description: The date of the payment reported on the summary, under the column name the payment summary tables use from 2018-19 onwards and in the 2009-10 extract before that. The years from 2010-11 to 2017-18 carry the same date under a different name, so a series across the whole collection has to bridge two columns. The date matters most for termination payments, where the return asks the taxpayer to write the payment date shown on the summary and the tax treatment turns on the year the payment falls in.
value_definition: A calendar date on the summary, filled for the payment summary types that report one discrete payment and blank on the rows that report a whole year of pay. It is the name used in the 2009-10 extract and again from 2018-19, and it is absent from the tables in between.
limitation: The renaming means a naive stack of the year tables produces two sparsely filled date columns rather than one, and a count of dated rows falls to zero at the join if only one name is kept. The date itself also does not identify the kind of payment; that is in the payment summary type column beside it.
rationale: The column carries the payment date in exactly the tables where the period payment date column is absent, and the ATO return instruction describes the payment date field that both columns hold.
evidence_quote: Write at Date of payment the payment date on your income statement or payment summary.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that this is the later name for the payment date field used in the earlier tables.

value_domain: Mesh block, ASGS main structure
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Mesh Blocks
variable_description: The mesh block containing the address the ATO held for the payee, the finest geography the payment summary tables carry. The ABS describes mesh blocks as "the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS" which "form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS)", designed to hold between 30 and 60 dwellings. The SA1 to SA4, LGA and state codes on the same row are this one mesh block aggregated upward.
value_definition: An eleven-digit ASGS mesh block code. The custodian labels it as the 2016 edition in the 2021-22 table, so the edition can differ from the boundaries used elsewhere in the same product.
limitation: A mesh block is a small area, not a household or a workplace. Two people at the same address share a mesh block with dozens of neighbours, and the address is the payee's, so the code says nothing about where the work was done. Because the label names a different ASGS edition from the geography tables, codes must not be compared across tables without a correspondence.
rationale: The ABS standard defines mesh blocks, their dwelling design range and their role as the building block from which the other geography columns on the row are formed.
evidence_quote: Mesh Blocks are the smallest geographic areas defined by the ABS and form the building blocks for the larger regions of the Australian Statistical Geography Standard (ASGS).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the code is a small-area building block for the coarser geography columns beside it.

value_domain: Statistical Area Level 1, ASGS main structure
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 1
variable_description: The SA1 containing the payee's address, the level the ABS designs for maximum detail without disclosing people. The ABS defines SA1s as "geographic areas built from whole Mesh Blocks" that "generally have a population of 200 to 800 people, and an average population of about 400 people". In the 2015-16 to 2018-19 years it is delivered in a separate geography table keyed to the person rather than inline with the payments.
value_definition: An eleven-digit ASGS code. The custodian labels the field as the 2011 edition in several tables while the geography tables are named for 2021, so the boundary vintage has to be checked per table.
limitation: SA1 counts are suppressed or unstable for small groups, so an income measure averaged at this level is dominated by noise in sparsely populated areas. The special purpose codes matter too: people in transit or with no fixed address sit in non-spatial SA1s that must be dropped before mapping, not treated as a location.
rationale: The ABS standard defines SA1s, their population range and the non-spatial special purpose codes that share the classification.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s) are geographic areas built from whole Mesh Blocks.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said how small an SA1 is or that non-spatial codes sit inside the same classification.

value_domain: Statistical Area Level 2, ASGS main structure
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 2
variable_description: The SA2 containing the payee's address, the level meant to stand for a community rather than a statistical unit. The ABS defines SA2s as "medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s)" whose "purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically". It is the level most PLIDA analysis settles on, because SA1 is too sparse for annual income measures and SA3 is too coarse for a suburb.
value_definition: A nine-digit ASGS code, one value per row, with 2,473 areas covering Australia including nineteen non-spatial special purpose codes.
limitation: An SA2 is a residence, not a labour market, so wages summed by this column measure where earners sleep rather than where the jobs are; the SA4 code on the same row is the labour market level. Boundaries also change between ASGS editions, so an SA2 series across the whole payment summary period needs a correspondence rather than a straight join.
rationale: The ABS standard defines SA2s, their purpose and their count, which is what distinguishes this column from the SA1 and SA3 codes beside it.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s) are medium-sized general purpose areas built up from whole Statistical Areas Level 1 (SA1s). Their purpose is to represent a community that interacts together socially and economically.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the SA2 is meant to represent a community and is the practical level for small-area income work.

value_domain: Statistical Area Level 3, ASGS main structure
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 3
variable_description: The SA3 containing the payee's address, the regional level used for comparing parts of a city or a state. The ABS defines SA3s as "geographic areas built from whole Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s)" designed "for the output of regional data" by "clustering groups of SA2s that have similar regional characteristics". It appears only in the 2021-22 and 2022-23 payment summary tables, which carry the full SA1 to SA4 ladder inline.
value_definition: A five-digit ASGS code that aggregates whole SA2s and in turn aggregates to SA4s.
limitation: The clustering is by regional character rather than by administration, so an SA3 is not a council, a service district or an electorate and cannot be used to attribute income to any of them. It is also absent from the earlier payment summary years, so an SA3 panel has to be built up from SA2 codes for those years rather than read off this column.
rationale: The ABS standard defines SA3s, how they are formed and what they are designed for, which separates them from the SA2 and SA4 codes on the same row.
evidence_quote: Statistical Areas Level 3 (SA3s) are geographic areas built from whole Statistical Areas Level 2 (SA2s).
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the SA3 is a regional grouping of SA2s available only in the later tables.

value_domain: Statistical Area Level 4, ASGS main structure
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Statistical Area Level 4
variable_description: The SA4 containing the payee's address, the largest sub-state region and the one built to stand for a labour market. The ABS states that "SA4 boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively" and designs them "with an emphasis on stability over time" to support the labour force series. Of the geography columns on a payment summary row, this is the one that lines up with published employment statistics.
value_definition: A three-digit ASGS code aggregating whole SA3s, designed to hold a large enough population to support labour force estimates.
limitation: It is still the payee's residence, not the workplace, so commuting flows are invisible and a capital city SA4 mixes people who work across the whole metropolitan area. The stability the ABS designs for is across time, not across editions, so codes from an earlier ASGS edition are not interchangeable with these.
rationale: The ABS standard states what SA4 boundaries represent and why they are designed for stability, which is what makes this the labour market level among the geography columns.
evidence_quote: SA4 boundaries represent labour markets and the functional area of Australian capital cities respectively.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the SA4 is the labour market level of the classification.

value_domain: State or territory, ASGS main structure
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Australia and State/Territory
variable_description: The state or territory of the payee's address, the coarsest of the geography columns on the row. The ABS builds the level from the areas below it: "States and Territories consist of one or more Statistical Areas Level 4 (SA4). In aggregate, they cover Australia without gaps or overlaps", and identifies each by a unique one-digit code. It is the only geography column present in every payment summary year, so a state series runs the full length of the collection.
value_definition: A one-digit ASGS state or territory code. The classification also carries codes for other territories and for the non-spatial categories that sit outside any state.
limitation: It is a statistical geography, not a tax jurisdiction: the payer's state is not recorded anywhere, so state-level payroll or wage analysis built from this column attributes pay to where the worker lives. A person who moves interstate mid-year is counted wholly in the state of the address the ATO held, with no indication that a move took place.
rationale: The ABS standard defines states and territories as an aggregation of SA4s and describes the one-digit coding, which is what this column carries.
evidence_quote: States and Territories consist of one or more Statistical Areas Level 4 (SA4). In aggregate, they cover Australia without gaps or overlaps.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the code is the ASGS aggregation of SA4s and refers to the payee's address rather than the payer's.

value_domain: Local government area, ASGS non-ABS structure
value_source: ABS, Australian Statistical Geography Standard Edition 3, Local Government Areas
variable_description: The council area of the address the ATO held for the payee when the payment summary was reported. The ABS builds it from small areas rather than from the legal boundary: "Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory." For 2015-16 to 2018-19 it arrives in a separate geography table keyed to the person, and from 2019-20 it sits inline with the payment amounts.
value_definition: A five-digit code, a one-digit state or territory identifier followed by a four-digit council identifier, built from whole mesh blocks and reissued as councils change.
limitation: It cannot support any claim about council finances or entitlements, since the ABS states these approximations "should only be used for statistical purposes". Unincorporated areas have no council at all, so rows there are not missing data, and a payee who moved between councils during the year is assigned entirely to the address on file.
rationale: The ABS standard defines local government areas as a mesh block approximation of gazetted boundaries and states the statistical-use limitation and the coding structure.
evidence_quote: Local Government Areas are an ABS Mesh Block approximation of gazetted local government boundaries as defined by each state and territory. ABS approximations of administrative boundaries do not match official legal boundaries and should only be used for statistical purposes.
supersedes_rationale: The entry carried the custodian's own label as its description and printed the generic no-value-list sentence as both the value definition and the limitation, so nothing on the page said that the boundaries approximate council areas from mesh blocks and describe the payee's home address.
